{{Short description|Exploitation of impossible differences in block ciphers}}
In [[cryptography]], '''impossible differential cryptanalysis''' is a form of [[differential cryptanalysis]] for [[block cipher]]s. While ordinary differential cryptanalysis tracks differences that propagate through the cipher with greater than expected [[probability]], impossible differential cryptanalysis exploits differences that are impossible (having probability 0) at some intermediate [[state (computer science)|state]] of the cipher algorithm.

[[Lars Ramkilde Knudsen|Lars Knudsen]] appears to be the first to use a form of this attack, in the 1998 paper where he introduced his [[Advanced Encryption Standard process|AES candidate]], [[DEAL]].<ref>{{ cite journal
| author = Lars Knudsen | title = DEAL - A 128-bit Block Cipher | version = Technical report no. 151
| publisher = Department of Informatics, [[University of Bergen]], Norway | date = February 21, 1998 | url =  http://www2.mat.dtu.dk/people/Lars.R.Knudsen/papers/deal.pdf.gz | access-date = 2015-05-28 }}</ref> The first presentation to attract the attention of the cryptographic community was later the same year at the rump session of [[CRYPTO]] '98, in which [[Eli Biham]], [[Alex Biryukov]], and [[Adi Shamir]] introduced the name "impossible differential"<ref>Shamir, A. (August 25, 1998) [http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=1283860161748060032&hl=en Impossible differential attacks.] CRYPTO '98 rump session (video at [[Google Video]]&mdash;uses [[Adobe Flash|Flash]])</ref> and used the technique to break 4.5 out of 8.5 rounds of [[International Data Encryption Algorithm|IDEA]]<ref>Biryukov, A. (August 25, 1998) [http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=-5370812042739937841&hl=en Miss-in-the-middle attacks on IDEA.] CRYPTO '98 rump session (video at Google Video&mdash;uses Flash)</ref> and 31 out of 32 rounds of the [[National Security Agency|NSA]]-designed cipher [[Skipjack (cipher)|Skipjack]].<ref>Biham, E. (August 25, 1998) [http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=-312957337727284112&hl=en Impossible cryptanalysis of Skipjack.] CRYPTO '98 rump session (video at Google Video&mdash;uses Flash)</ref> This development led cryptographer [[Bruce Schneier]] to speculate that the NSA had no previous knowledge of impossible differential cryptanalysis.<ref>{{ Cite journal | author = Bruce Schneier | title = Impossible Cryptanalysis and Skipjack | journal = Crypto-Gram Newsletter | date = September 15, 1998 | url = https://www.schneier.com/crypto-gram-9809.html#impossible }}</ref> The technique has since been applied to many other ciphers: [[Khufu and Khafre]], [[E2 (cipher)|E2]], variants of [[Serpent (cipher)|Serpent]], [[MARS (cryptography)|MARS]], [[Twofish]], [[Rijndael]] (AES), [[CRYPTON]], [[Zodiac (cipher)|Zodiac]], [[Hierocrypt-3]], [[Tiny Encryption Algorithm|TEA]], [[XTEA]], [[Mini-AES]], [[ARIA (cipher)|ARIA]], [[Camellia (cipher)|Camellia]], and [[SHACAL-2]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

Biham, Biryukov and Shamir also presented a relatively efficient specialized method for finding impossible differentials that they called a ''miss-in-the-middle'' attack. This consists of finding "two events with probability one, whose conditions cannot be met together."<ref>{{ cite conference | author1 = E. Biham | author2 = A. Biryukov | author3 = A. Shamir | title = Miss in the Middle Attacks on IDEA, Khufu and Khafre | conference = 6th International Workshop on [[Fast Software Encryption]] (FSE 1999) | pages = 124–138 | publisher = [[Springer-Verlag]] | date = March 1999 | location = Rome | url = http://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~albi/fse99idea.ps.gz | format = [[gzip]]ped PostScript | access-date = 2007-02-14 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110515085818/http://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~albi/fse99idea.ps.gz | archive-date = 2011-05-15 }}</ref>
